subject: biology
topicDisplay: Theme D · Ecosystems (Natural Selection, Stability, Climate Change)
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Natural selection acts on variation that is:
questions.explain: Only heritable variation can be passed to offspring and change allele frequencies over generations.

questions.q: In evolutionary terms, an individual's fitness refers to its:
questions.explain: Fitness is the ability to survive and reproduce, passing on alleles to the next generation.

questions.q: The increase in dark peppered moths during industrial pollution is a classic example of:
options: Natural selection through a changed environment
questions.explain: Dark moths were better camouflaged on soot-darkened trees, so they survived and reproduced more.

questions.q: A selection pressure is:
options: An environmental factor that affects survival and reproduction
questions.explain: Selection pressures (e.g. predators, climate, disease) favour some phenotypes over others.

questions.q: Antibiotic resistance spreads because antibiotics:
options: Select for resistant bacteria that survive and reproduce
Cause bacteria to become resistant on demand
questions.explain: Resistant variants already present survive antibiotic treatment and pass on resistance alleles.

questions.q: A stable ecosystem is one that:
options: Maintains its structure and function over time despite disturbances
questions.explain: Stability involves resistance to change and the ability to recover (resilience) after disturbance.

questions.q: Higher biodiversity tends to make an ecosystem:
questions.explain: Greater diversity provides more functional redundancy, helping ecosystems absorb and recover from change.

questions.q: Removing a keystone species from a community often causes:
questions.explain: Keystone species have effects out of proportion to their abundance, so their loss can restructure the community.

questions.q: A tipping point in an ecosystem refers to:
options: A threshold beyond which change becomes rapid and hard to reverse
questions.explain: Crossing a tipping point (e.g. coral reef collapse) can shift an ecosystem to a very different state.

questions.q: The main greenhouse gas released by human combustion of fossil fuels is:
questions.explain: Rising atmospheric CO2 (and methane) enhances the greenhouse effect, driving global warming.

questions.q: The enhanced greenhouse effect leads to global warming because greenhouse gases:
questions.explain: Greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit infrared radiation, warming the lower atmosphere.

questions.q: Rising sea temperatures cause coral bleaching because corals:
options: Expel their symbiotic algae, losing colour and a food source
questions.explain: Heat stress breaks the coral–zooxanthellae symbiosis, and prolonged bleaching can kill the coral.

questions.q: Increased atmospheric carbon dioxide dissolving in seawater causes:
questions.explain: Dissolved CO2 forms carbonic acid, lowering ocean pH and hindering shell and coral formation.

questions.q: A documented biological effect of climate change is:
options: Shifts in species distributions towards the poles or higher altitudes
Species remaining exactly where they were
questions.explain: Warming shifts ranges and alters the timing of events (phenology) such as flowering and migration.

questions.q: Which best describes the role of variation in natural selection?
options: It provides the differences on which selection can act
questions.explain: Without heritable variation, selection has nothing to act on and populations cannot adapt.

questions.q: Sexual selection can lead to features such as the peacock's tail because they:
options: Increase mating success even if they reduce survival
questions.explain: Traits that raise reproductive success can be favoured even at some survival cost.

questions.q: Ecosystem resilience is best described as the ability to:
questions.explain: Resilient ecosystems return towards their original state after disturbance, aided by biodiversity.

questions.q: The primary human cause of the current rise in atmospheric carbon dioxide is:
questions.explain: Combustion releases stored carbon while deforestation reduces CO2 uptake, together raising atmospheric CO2.

questions.q: Adaptations are features that:
options: Increase an organism's chance of survival and reproduction in its environment
Always appear within one lifetime by choice
questions.explain: Adaptations arise through natural selection acting on heritable variation over many generations.

questions.q: Warming that causes flowers to bloom before their pollinators emerge is an example of:
questions.explain: Climate change can desynchronise interacting species (e.g. plants and pollinators), harming both.
